claims.text: The damaged metallic components are susceptible to hot cracking when repaired by fusion welding.
The damaged surfaces have coarse-grained microstructures.
The untreated surfaces have insufficient resistance to aggressive environments.
Friction stir processing can incorporate pre-alloyed wear-resistant particles such as tungsten carbide into the near-surface region.
Friction stir processing is conducted below the melting point and therefore avoids complete melting.
The proposed treatment will produce a fine, nanostructured surface layer.
The proposed treatment will produce a homogeneous distribution of reinforcing particles in the processed layer.
The proposed treatment will refine the grains in the near-surface region.
Avoiding complete melting through solid-state processing minimizes thermal cracking.
Incorporated wear-resistant particles increase surface hardness.
Particle reinforcement and grain refinement inhibit crack nucleation and propagation.
The FSP-treated surface will have lower hot-cracking susceptibility than a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The FSP-treated surface will have higher hardness than a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The FSP-treated surface will have greater wear resistance than a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The FSP-treated surface will have greater corrosion resistance than a traditional fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The proposed treatment will extend component service life.
The intervention is effective only where component surfaces are accessible to the FSP tool and service conditions remain within the processed layer's thermal and mechanical limits.
Highly complex geometries or service conditions beyond tested limits may reduce the intervention's efficacy.
